Hilbert keys and spatial sorting

Source: R/kernel.R
geo_hilbert.Rd

geo_hilbert() maps each geometry's box centre onto a 2^16 by 2^16 grid over extent and gives its index along the Hilbert curve, with flatbush's arithmetic exactly, so a zugeo sort and a flatbush index agree (design section 6.7). Null and empty geometries have NA. geo_sort() gives the permutation that orders x by key, nulls and empties last, ties in their original order: x[geo_sort(x)] is the sorted vector.

Usage

geo_hilbert(x, extent = NULL, lossy = c("error", "warn", "allow"))

geo_sort(x, by = "hilbert", lossy = c("error", "warn", "allow"))

Arguments

x

A geo_vctr.

extent

NULL for the box around x, or a geo_extent of length one. Centres outside it are clamped onto its edge.

lossy

As for geo_box().

by

The sort key; "hilbert" is the one there is.

Value

geo_hilbert(): a double vector of unsigned 32-bit keys. geo_sort(): an integer permutation.

Examples

x <- geo_points(c(5, 1, 3), c(5, 1, 3))
geo_hilbert(x)
#> [1] 2863311530          0  715827882
geo_sort(x)
#> [1] 2 3 1
